svg.title: SIS vs SIR — resampling in the particle filter
svg.desc: Without resampling, SIS degenerates as weight concentrates on one particle; SIR redraws when the effective sample size drops below a threshold, restoring balance but losing diversity.
svg.text: SIS vs SIR — resampling in the particle filter
Updating weights until collapse vs redrawing periodically to survive
The variance of the weights explodes
Systematic or stratified, plus a move step
The rest cost computation but contribute nothing
Resampling makes the weights uniform again
Weights are even again, but positions are duplicated
Effective sample size falls to the floor
In this state the estimator's variance is out of control
refill whenever it touches the line
but particles sharing one ancestor multiply
SIS only updates weights and eventually degenerates to a single particle.
SIR redraws to restore balance, at the cost of duplicated particles and lost diversity.
The unbiased likelihood from a particle filter
Next: smoothing rules in practice are special cases of state space.
